{{Article header|deck=Laser mining uses mining lasers, collectors, and a refinery to turn asteroid fragments into cargo.}}

'''Laser mining''' is the most direct mining method: a ship fires [[Mining Laser|mining lasers]] at a suitable asteroid, uses [[Collector Limpet Controller|collector limpets]] to retrieve fragments, and relies on a [[Refinery]] to convert those fragments into cargo.

{{Draft warning}}

== When to use laser mining ==

Laser mining is the simplest method to learn because the extraction tool, collection loop, and refinery loop are all visible and repeatable. It is a good first mining style when the commander wants to understand limpets, refinery bins, cargo planning, and asteroid prospecting before adding core or sub-surface timing mechanics.

Laser mining is not automatically the most profitable choice. Commodity prices, demand, hotspot quality, and ship fit all matter, so this page avoids permanent sell-station recommendations.

== Equipment ==

For a basic laser-mining fit, focus on:

* [[Mining Laser]] — breaks ordinary asteroid fragments loose.
* [[Prospector Limpet Controller]] — reveals asteroid contents before time is spent mining.
* [[Collector Limpet Controller]] — retrieves fragments efficiently.
* [[Refinery]] — converts fragments into cargo.
* [[Cargo Rack|Cargo racks]] and limpets — provide both ammunition and space for the refined result.
* [[Detailed Surface Scanner]] — useful when choosing or confirming a mapped hotspot.

{{#invoke:Mining|equipmentTable}}

== Workflow summary ==

# Map or travel to a suitable ring or hotspot.
# Launch a [[Prospector Limpet Controller|prospector limpet]] at candidate asteroids before spending time on them.
# Mine useful asteroids with mining lasers while keeping collector limpets active.
# Watch refinery bins and cargo capacity so fragments do not block the process.
# Before selling, check current market demand and prices rather than relying on old route advice.

== Practical notes ==

* Launch collectors without targeting a single fragment unless a one-use pickup is intended.
* Keep some distance from the asteroid surface; limpets die quickly when they repeatedly collide with rock.
* A full cargo hold or blocked refinery can stop useful collection even while fragments are still floating nearby.
* Hotspots improve targeting, but every asteroid still needs to be prospected.
